title: TN Visa Quarterly Estimated Tax Calculator for RSUs: Avoid $5K+ Penalties 2026
description: Master quarterly estimated tax payments for TN visa holders with RSU income. Learn IRS safe harbor rules, payment deadlines, and strategies to avoid underpayment penalties.
content:
## Key Takeaways

- **RSUs create tax underpayment** - 22% withholding often insufficient (actual rate 28-37%)
- Quarterly estimated tax deadlines: **April 15, June 15, Sept 15, Jan 15**
- Safe harbor: Pay **110% of prior year tax** OR **90% of current year** - avoid penalties
- Average penalty for missing payments: **$2,500-$8,000** for tech workers with $200K+ RSUs
- Use our [free calculator](/us-canada-tax-calculator) to calculate exact quarterly payments

## Why TN Visa Holders Need Quarterly Estimated Tax

### The RSU Withholding Problem

When your RSUs vest, your employer automatically withholds:
- **Federal:** 22% (flat supplemental rate)
- **State:** 0-13.3% depending on state
- **FICA:** 7.65% (Social Security + Medicare)

But if your total income exceeds $191,950 (2026 single filer), your actual federal tax rate is **32%** - leaving a **10% shortfall**.

**Example:**
- Salary: $150,000
- RSUs vesting: $200,000
- Total income: $350,000

**Withholding:**
- Salary: $150K × 24% = $36,000
- RSUs: $200K × 22% = $44,000
- **Total withheld: $80,000**

**Actual tax owed:**
- $350K at ~28% effective = **$98,000**

**Shortfall:**
- $98,000 - $80,000 = **$18,000 underpaid**

**Penalty:**
- IRS charges **5% annual interest** on underpayment
- Calculated quarterly, compounded
- **Average penalty: $450-$900/year** (depending on timing)

### Who Must Make Quarterly Estimated Payments

**Required if:**
- You expect to owe **>$1,000** when you file your return
- Your withholding + credits will be **<90%** of current year tax OR **<100%** of prior year tax

**Not required if:**
- Your withholding covers >90% of current year tax
- You paid >110% of prior year tax (via withholding + estimates)
- You had zero tax liability last year (new to US)

**TN visa workers typically need estimates if:**
- ✅ Large RSU vesting ($100K+)
- ✅ Mid-year RSU refresh grants
- ✅ Stock price increased significantly (more shares vest than expected)
- ✅ Side income (consulting, freelance)
- ✅ Investment income (dividends, interest >$10K)

## IRS Safe Harbor Rules Explained

### What Is "Safe Harbor"?

Safe harbor = **No penalties** even if you underpay, as long as you meet one of these tests:

**Test 1: 90% of Current Year Tax**

Pay at least 90% of your 2026 tax liability by Jan 15, 2027 (via withholding + estimates).

**Example:**
- 2026 tax: $100,000
- Safe harbor: $90,000
- If you paid $91,000 → **No penalty** (even though you owe $9,000)

**Test 2: 100% of Prior Year Tax (or 110% if high income)**

Pay 100% of your 2025 tax (or 110% if 2025 AGI > $150,000).

**Example:**
- 2025 tax: $80,000
- 2025 AGI: $200,000 → Use **110%** rule
- Safe harbor: $88,000
- If you paid $88,000 in 2026 → **No penalty** (even if 2026 tax is $120,000)

**Which to use?**

**Use Test 1 (90% current year) if:**
- Income decreased (layoff, sabbatical)
- Stock price dropped (fewer RSU value)

**Use Test 2 (110% prior year) if:**
- Income increased significantly
- Large RSU vesting in current year
- You want certainty (easy to calculate from last year's return)

**Best practice:** Calculate both, pay the **lower** amount to minimize cash outlay.

### Quarterly Deadlines and Payment Allocation

**IRS divides the year into 4 periods:**

| Period | Income Earned | Payment Due | Form |
|--------|---------------|-------------|------|
| Q1 | Jan 1 - Mar 31 | April 15 | 1040-ES |
| Q2 | Apr 1 - May 31 | June 15 | 1040-ES |
| Q3 | June 1 - Aug 31 | Sept 15 | 1040-ES |
| Q4 | Sept 1 - Dec 31 | Jan 15 (next year) | 1040-ES |

**Key dates for TN visa holders:**
- **April 15:** Q1 payment + prior year return due
- **June 15:** Q2 payment (45 days after quarter ends)
- **Sept 15:** Q3 payment
- **Jan 15:** Q4 payment OR increase W-4 withholding

**Pro Tip:** If you miss a quarterly deadline, you **can't make it up** by paying more in the next quarter. The penalty applies to the specific quarter you underpaid.

## Calculating Your Quarterly Estimated Tax

### Method 1: 110% Prior Year Safe Harbor (Simplest)

**Step 1:** Find your 2025 total tax
- Form 1040, Line 24: $80,000

**Step 2:** Multiply by 110% (if AGI >$150K)
- $80,000 × 110% = **$88,000**

**Step 3:** Subtract withholding already paid
- 2026 W-2 withholding (salary only): $36,000
- RSU withholding (projected): $44,000
- **Total: $80,000**

**Step 4:** Calculate quarterly payment needed
- Safe harbor: $88,000
- Already withheld: $80,000
- **Total estimates needed: $8,000**
- Per quarter: $8,000 ÷ 4 = **$2,000**

**Result:** Pay $2,000 by Apr 15, June 15, Sept 15, Jan 15.

### Method 2: 90% Current Year (More Complex, Lower Payment)

**Step 1:** Project 2026 income
- Salary: $150,000
- RSUs vesting: $200,000
- **Total: $350,000**

**Step 2:** Calculate projected tax
- Use [IRS tax calculator](https://www.irs.gov/forms-pubs/about-form-1040-es)
- Or our [free calculator](/us-canada-tax-calculator)
- **Projected tax: $98,000**

**Step 3:** Apply 90% safe harbor
- $98,000 × 90% = **$88,200**

**Step 4:** Subtract withholding
- Already withheld: $80,000
- **Estimates needed: $8,200**
- Per quarter: $2,050

**Compare to Method 1:**
- Method 1 (110% prior): $8,000
- Method 2 (90% current): $8,200
- **Winner: Method 1** (pay $200 less)

### Method 3: Annualized Income (for Uneven Income)

If your RSUs vest unevenly (e.g., $150K in Q1, $0 in Q2-Q4), you can use the **annualized income installment method** to pay based on actual income each quarter.

**Example:**

**Q1:** RSUs vest $150K
- Q1 income: $150K
- Annualized: $150K × 4 = $600K
- Tax: $600K × 35% = $210K
- Q1 payment: $210K × 25% = **$52,500** (due Apr 15)

**Q2-Q4:** No RSUs, salary only ($37.5K each)
- Q2 income: $37.5K
- Cumulative (Q1+Q2): $187.5K
- Annualized: $187.5K × 2 = $375K
- Tax: $375K × 32% = $120K
- Already paid Q1: $52,500
- Q2 payment: ($120K × 50%) - $52,500 = **$7,500** (due June 15)

**This method reduces cash flow burden** but requires filing **Form 2210** with your return.

**Best for:**
- RSUs vest in one big tranche (year-end bonuses)
- You leave your job mid-year (income drops)
- Stock price crashes (vesting value drops)

## Real Example: Microsoft TN Visa Engineer

**Profile:**
- David, TN visa at Microsoft Redmond
- Salary: $180,000/year
- RSU vesting: $220,000/year (quarterly vests)
- Total comp: $400,000

**Mistake:** David thought 22% withholding was enough.

**What actually happened:**

**2025 Tax Year:**
- Total income: $400,000
- Actual tax: $112,000 (28% effective)
- Withholding: $88,000 (22% on RSUs)
- **Shortfall: $24,000**

**April 15, 2026: Tax filing**
- Owed: $24,000
- Penalty: $1,200 (5% for underpayment)
- Interest: $600
- **Total due: $25,800**

**2026 (fixed with quarterly estimates):**

**Q1 (Jan-Mar):**
- RSU vest: $55,000 (March)
- Withholding: $12,100 (22%)
- Estimated payment: $5,000 (paid Apr 15)

**Q2 (Apr-May):**
- RSU vest: $55,000 (June)
- Withholding: $12,100
- Estimated payment: $5,000 (paid June 15)

**Q3 (June-Aug):**
- RSU vest: $55,000 (Sept)
- Withholding: $12,100
- Estimated payment: $5,000 (paid Sept 15)

**Q4 (Sept-Dec):**
- RSU vest: $55,000 (Dec)
- Withholding: $12,100
- Estimated payment: $5,000 (paid Jan 15, 2027)

**Total paid:**
- Withholding: $88,000
- Estimates: $20,000
- **Total: $108,000**

**Tax owed (2026 filing):**
- Total tax: $112,000
- Paid: $108,000
- **Owe: $4,000** (within safe harbor, no penalty)

**Savings:** $1,200 penalty + $600 interest = **$1,800**

## State Estimated Tax (CA, NY, MA)

### California Estimated Tax

California requires quarterly payments if you expect to owe **>$500**.

**Deadlines:** Same as federal (Apr 15, June 15, Sept 15, Jan 15)

**Safe harbor:**
- 90% of current year tax OR
- 100% of prior year tax (110% if AGI >$150K)

**Payment methods:**
- Online: [CA FTB Web Pay](https://webapp.ftb.ca.gov/webpay/)
- Mail: Form 540-ES voucher

**Example:**
- 2025 CA tax: $35,000
- 2026 AGI: $400,000 → Use 110% rule
- Safe harbor: $38,500
- Already withheld: $36,000 (9% on RSUs)
- **Quarterly estimates: $2,500 total** ($625/quarter)

### New York Estimated Tax

**Same rules as federal:**
- 90% current year OR 110% prior year (if AGI >$150K)

**NYC residents:** Must also pay NYC estimated tax (separate from NY state)

**Deadlines:** April 15, June 15, Sept 15, Jan 15

**Payment:** [NY Tax.gov](https://www8.tax.ny.gov/PAYB/)

### Washington State - No Estimated Tax

WA has **no state income tax** → No quarterly estimates needed.

**But watch out:**
- WA has **capital gains tax** on stock sales >$250K/year (7% rate)
- Applies to RSU sales (not vesting)
- Estimated payments required if selling >$250K stocks

## Strategies to Avoid Quarterly Payments

### Strategy 1: Increase W-4 Withholding (Easier Than Estimates)

**How it works:**
- Instead of paying quarterly estimates, have employer withhold more from salary
- Adjust W-4 Form, Line 4(c) - "Extra withholding"

**Advantage over estimates:**
- IRS treats withholding as **paid evenly throughout year** (even if withheld in December)
- Estimates must be paid quarterly or face penalty

**Example:**
- You owe $20,000 more tax
- Option A: Pay $5,000 quarterly (4 payments, track deadlines)
- Option B: Increase W-4 by $833/month (automatic, no deadlines)

**To calculate extra withholding:**
1. Estimate total tax shortfall: $20,000
2. Divide by remaining paychecks: $20,000 ÷ 24 = $833
3. Update W-4, Line 4(c): "$833"

**Pro Tip:** If you realize in December you underpaid, you can **increase W-4 for December** to catch up (IRS treats it as paid all year).

### Strategy 2: Sell RSU Shares to Cover Tax

At vesting, your employer offers "sell-to-cover" option:

**How it works:**
- RSUs vest: 1,000 shares @ $100 = $100,000
- Tax owed: ~$37,000 (37% marginal)
- Platform auto-sells: 370 shares
- You keep: 630 shares

**Advantage:**
- No out-of-pocket cash needed
- No quarterly estimates (tax covered at source)

**Disadvantage:**
- Locks in stock price at vesting
- If stock rises 50% next month, you missed gains on 370 shares

**Best for:**
- Risk-averse workers (don't want to owe tax later)
- Concentrated positions (already >20% net worth in company stock)

### Strategy 3: Contribute to Pre-Tax Retirement Accounts

Reduce taxable income → reduce estimated payments.

**Options for TN visa holders:**
- **401(k):** $23,000 limit (2026)
- **Traditional IRA:** $7,000 limit (but phased out if income >$78,000 single)
- **Mega backdoor Roth:** Up to $70,000 (if employer plan allows)

**Example:**
- Income: $400,000
- Max 401(k): $23,000
- Taxable income: $377,000
- Tax saved: $23,000 × 35% = **$8,050**
- Estimated payment reduced: $2,012/quarter

**Catch:** Must contribute **during the year** (not retroactive). Can't wait until April to reduce prior year income.

### Strategy 4: Bunch Deductions in High-Income Years

If you itemize deductions:

**Accelerate deductions:**
- Pay Jan 2027 mortgage → in Dec 2026 (double deduction)
- Make charitable donations in Dec 2026 (instead of Jan 2027)
- Pay state estimated tax in Dec 2026 (deduct in 2026)

**Example:**
- 2026 income: $400,000 (high)
- 2027 income: $200,000 (sabbatical)
- Bunch $40,000 deductions into 2026
- Tax saved: $40,000 × 35% = **$14,000** (vs 24% in 2027 = $9,600)
- **Extra savings: $4,400**

## Penalties for Underpayment

### How IRS Calculates Penalty

IRS charges **5% annual interest** (compounded quarterly) on underpayment.

**Formula:**
```
Penalty = (Tax owed - Tax paid) × 5% × (Days late / 365)
```

**Example:**
- Q1 payment due: April 15
- You paid: $0 (forgot)
- Should have paid: $5,000
- You paid on Sept 15 (153 days late)

**Penalty:**
- $5,000 × 5% × (153 / 365) = **$105**

**If you miss all 4 quarters:**
- Q1: $105 (153 days late)
- Q2: $75 (92 days late)
- Q3: $50 (61 days late)
- Q4: $25 (30 days late)
- **Total: $255** (on $5,000 underpayment)

**For high earners:**
- Underpayment: $30,000
- **Penalty: ~$1,500-$3,000** (depending on timing)

### Form 2210: Underpayment Penalty Calculation

If you underpaid, IRS sends Form 2210 calculating penalty.

**You can reduce/eliminate penalty by:**

**1. Claiming safe harbor:**
- Check box on Form 2210: "You paid 110% of prior year tax"
- IRS waives penalty automatically

**2. Casualty/disaster:**
- Hurricane, wildfire destroyed home → reasonable cause
- IRS waives penalty (attach explanation)

**3. Annualized income method:**
- File Form 2210, Schedule AI
- Show income was uneven (high in Q4, low in Q1-Q3)
- Reduce penalty for Q1-Q3

**4. First-time penalty abatement:**
- If you've never been penalized before (3-year lookback)
- IRS grants **one-time forgiveness** (call IRS: 1-800-829-1040)

## Action Checklist

**Before Q1 deadline (April 15):**
- [ ] Calculate 2026 projected tax using our [free calculator](/us-canada-tax-calculator)
- [ ] Determine safe harbor amount (110% prior year vs 90% current year)
- [ ] Subtract 2026 withholding already paid (salary W-4)
- [ ] Calculate quarterly payment needed: (Safe harbor - withholding) ÷ 4
- [ ] Set calendar reminders for deadlines (Apr 15, June 15, Sept 15, Jan 15)

**Payment methods:**
- [ ] Online: [IRS Direct Pay](https://www.irs.gov/payments/direct-pay) (free)
- [ ] EFTPS (Electronic Federal Tax Payment System) - register in advance
- [ ] Mail: Form 1040-ES voucher with check
- [ ] Credit card: 1.85-1.99% fee (not recommended)

**Alternative to quarterly payments:**
- [ ] Update W-4 to increase withholding (easier than tracking deadlines)
- [ ] Calculate extra withholding: Total shortfall ÷ remaining paychecks
- [ ] Submit new W-4 to employer payroll (Line 4(c) - extra withholding)

**If you miss a payment:**
- [ ] Pay ASAP (reduces penalty interest)
- [ ] Don't skip future quarters (each quarter compounds penalty)
- [ ] File Form 2210 with return explaining late payment
- [ ] Request first-time penalty abatement (if eligible)

**When filing tax return:**
- [ ] Report estimated payments on Form 1040, Line 26
- [ ] Keep payment confirmation receipts (proof of payment)
- [ ] If penalized, file Form 2210 claiming safe harbor or annualized income
